Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways + Reactome), mummichog m/z-direct network analysis on the human metabolic-function network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA — converge on a single biological axis: androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently scores KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) at p=8.39e-06 with the same five driver steroids. react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by a coordinated shift in steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways + Reactome), mummichog m/z-direct network analysis on the human metabolic-function network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA — converge on a single biological axis: androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP identifies the SMPDB Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068) and the equivalent KEGG map00150 as the top hits (FDR 5.73e-15, fold-enrichment 1429×), with five driver steroids (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and 17β-estradiol) hitting 5 of 27 pathway members. Mummichog independently recovers the same biological process with complete network overlap (11/11 compounds), confirming that the mass-signals are biochemically coherent. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently scores KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) at p=8.39e-06 with the same five driver steroids. Within this axis, dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227) and androstenedione (C00280) are canonical upstream precursors to testosterone (C00535), which is further reduced to 5α-dihydrotestosterone (C03917) by 5α-reductase; the parallel estrogen arm is represented by 17β-estradiol (C00951), which is synthesised from testosterone via aromatase. The consistent perturbation of the complete C19 steroid backbone simultaneously across androgen and estrogen branches, observed in both ORA and network-diffusion paradigms, indicates a systemic disruption of steroidogenesis — mechanistically consistent with altered CYP17A1, aromatase, or 5α-reductase activity. Butan-2-one and sulindac do not appear in any pathway hit list, indicating they are not connected to the steroidogenesis axis in this dataset.
